about: Trust notes for each test run, written by hand after looking at its graphs. combine_usage.py copies them into container-usage.json. trust is one of: good, caveats, low.
all_runs: Each size has only one test run, so how much its numbers would vary between runs is unknown. The runs also weren't set up the same way: three OpenShift versions (4.19, 4.20, 4.22), four kube-burner versions (1.6.9, 1.7.9, 1.8.0, 1.11.12), a 30-second or 2-minute churn delay, and churn phases that actually lasted 20 to 63 minutes (most were set to 20), so comparing sizes partly compares setups. The shortest churn phases (20 to 23 minutes: 3, 6 and 12 nodes at 100 QPS, 30 and 49 nodes) give few 5-minute averages, so their CPU p95 is close to the highest value.

3-node-aro-hcp.notes: Memory is complete, but only 74% of CPU readings exist, so its CPU numbers, especially peaks, are less reliable. Its CPU graph marks the moments that read low, and its totals fill in the missing readings. Runs a newer OpenShift (4.20) than most runs (4.19).

6-node-aro-hcp.notes: Only 72% of CPU readings exist and a few memory readings are missing, so its CPU numbers, especially peaks, are less reliable. Its graphs mark the moments that read low, and its totals fill in the missing readings. Runs a newer OpenShift (4.20) than most runs (4.19).

12-nodes-20-client-qps-rate-aro-hcp.notes: Complete data. Its churn phase was set to 30 minutes instead of the usual 20, and an earlier kube-apiserver rollout was just finishing as churn began (the last old copy's last reading is 12 seconds into it), which barely affects the numbers.

12-nodes-100-client-qps-rate-aro-hcp.notes: Complete data. Set to 100 QPS, but kube-burner only reached about 6 queries per second, against about 4.7 in the 20 QPS run, so its load was only a little higher. Uses about 2 GiB more memory than the other 12-node run, mostly kube-apiserver.

49-node-hcp-raw.notes: Complete data, but a different setup from the other runs: newer OpenShift (4.22, most runs are 4.19) and kube-burner (1.11.12) versions, and the only run with a router. Uses more memory than the 60-node run.

60-node-aro-hcp.notes: Complete data, with a long churn phase (36 minutes).

120-node-aro-hcp.notes: Complete data, with a long churn phase (33 minutes).

250-node-aro-hcp.notes: Complete once its duplicate records are removed, which the scripts do, with a long churn phase (63 minutes).

500-node-aro-hcp.notes: No churn phase, and memory climbs until near the end: memory comes from its last 10 minutes, once it has leveled off, and CPU from the whole run, which is all create phase and so a conservative (high) estimate. The memory may be a few percent low, as in the large runs (60 to 250 nodes) churn-phase memory was 0 to 8% above the end of their create phase. Ran with 498 workers. Its duplicate records are removed by the scripts.
